verdict.rationale: Braintrust explicitly advertises scoring outputs with code. Its SDKs take a `scores` array in `Eval(...)` and provide scorer constructors, such as a trace-assertion scorer in the TypeScript SDK. Scorers are first-class objects that can be managed via the API and authored through MCP, and they produce numeric scores alongside label-assigning classifiers. Missing for 10: a documented example of a user-written custom scorer function (the GitHub example uses the built-in LevenshteinScorer), details on scorer signatures and return formats, and independent hands-on corroboration of custom scorer authoring.
